entry.title: apic: a command line for any HTTP API, without writing a CLI per service
entry.summary:
apic turns any HTTP API into a command line tool: it reads the API definition (OpenAPI / Swagger, or a few lines of YAML) and builds one command per endpoint, with parameters as options and shell completion.
Definitions become commands: a service with an OpenAPI document is one site add away; for an internal service without one, list its endpoints in a few lines of YAML. apic link also gives a site its own command, such as petctl. Environments and authentication: separate base URLs and credentials for dev and prod; bearer, basic, apikey, log-in-for-a-token and token-from-a-command auth; writes to production need --yes. Picking, paging, formatting: --pick takes fields from any level and renames them, --all-pages walks and merges the pages, -o table / yaml makes the result readable. For people and AI agents: stdout carries only the response body, exit codes have fixed meanings, and apic skill writes a SKILL.md for agents. Secrets are masked in -v, --dry-run and error messages. …
